Best vape to get with $200 budget. Suggestions?
Portable or tabletop? Dry herbs or wax?

I have a lot of experience with vaporizers as I have bought 6 of them over the past few years. Sorry this is long.... wake and bake. ☺️

My Advice:

  1. Decide whether you want a portable vape or a table to vape. Basically you are looking at how you want to be vaporizing are you look to sit in the circle and toke or are you looking for something you can use on the go.
  2. Decide wether you want a convection vape or a conduction vape. It may be a personal preference, but I prefer convection.
  3. Decide if you have a preference between bud and oil.
  4. Find a unit in your price ranch that fits with the decisions you have made above and try it out.

Other things to consider are the battery life, recharging time, weight, looks, etc.

If you mostly smoke at home I recommend a table top version. Portable units are restricted by the bowl size and battery life. As such, if you are going to be smoking alone they work great. If you plan on showing off the unit to your buddies, you may find that with 3 people the unit is not as effective. However, portable oil vapes can be more efficient, which makes sharing more practical. I have a personal preference for bud vapes because I am a silly purist; I do not trust the manufactured oils. However, many of my friends love oil vapes because they are simple and work. As such, if you have a preference for oils you may not want to go with a table top vape.

I highly recommend the Arizer Air for portable use. I own two and both have worked great. It is a convection vape, 1 g (or less) of bud is placed in the mouth piece, you can select your temperature in intervals of 5 degrees celsius, and the battery life is sufficient for 5-6 , 10 minute cycles. However, the company needs a bit more staff in their customer service department, it took a while for them to get back to me regarding some of my questions. The same company sells a very good table top convection vaporizer that can be used for balloons or a whip. I own one and I use it the most.

I do not recommend going with the firefly. I previously owned a firefly. The concept and design are great, however, the functionality of the vaporizer is lost due to the shitty battery life and the long recharging time. I complained to the company in an attempt to obtain a refund or at least a new battery. After much argument they agreed to look at the unit free of charge (they wanted to charge me to ship it to them and pay a 50% restocking fee if I wanted to return the unit). After, 3 weeks they sent it back with a new battery. After using it a couple times, I was still disappointed and found no difference in the battery life. I subsequently sold it and decided to buy a second Arizer Air with the cash.

Last thing, shop around. When my father-in-law bought an Arizer Extreme Q, he saved $60 and got free 2 day shipping when he purchased from a online vape store rather from the from the manufacture, which is what I had done. 😒

Hope this helps.
